sourceNote: Core sites from Wikipedia Geosearch API. City Palace, Fateh Sagar Lake, Sajjangarh, Bagore Ki Haveli show and craft village added as curated records. All records needs_review.

places.name: Lake Pichola
places.description: 4km-long artificial lake created in 1362, the centrepiece of Udaipur's romantic landscape. Boat rides depart from Rameshwar Ghat and Bansi Ghat, passing by the Lake Palace and Jag Mandir. Best viewed at sunset from the Ambrai Ghat or the City Palace terrace. No entry fee for the lakefront; boat rides are ticketed.

places.name: City Palace, Udaipur
places.description: Massive palace complex built over three centuries (1553 onwards) rising 30m above Lake Pichola. The largest palace complex in Rajasthan; features ornate balconies, peacock courtyards, mirror work and Lake Palace views. Museum wing (Zenana Mahal) open to visitors. Budget 2–3 hours for the full complex.

places.name: Lake Palace
places.description: 18th-century white marble palace built 1746 on a small island in Lake Pichola, now a luxury Taj hotel. Accessible only by boat from the City Palace jetty. Non-guests can visit for high tea or dinner with advance reservation. The exterior view from the lake shore is free and spectacular.
places.openingDays: Open to guests of Taj Hotel; non-guests need reservation

places.name: Jag Mandir Palace
places.description: 17th-century pleasure palace on a small island at the southern end of Lake Pichola, accessible by boat from the City Palace jetty (entry ticket includes boat). The garden contains the Gul Mahal pavilion and ornate elephant statues. Prince Khurram (later Shah Jahan) sheltered here while in rebellion against his father.

places.name: Fateh Sagar Lake
places.description: Artificial lake north of the city, constructed in 1678 and rebuilt after dam collapse in 1889. Features Nehru Park (island garden), a solar observatory, and a public park along the embankment. Boat rides available; popular for evening promenades and cycling along Fateh Sagar Road. Free lakefront access.

places.name: Sajjangarh Palace (Monsoon Palace)
places.description: White marble hilltop palace built in 1884 by Maharana Sajjan Singh, originally intended as a monsoon cloud observatory. Now offers the best panoramic view over Udaipur's lakes and city, especially at sunset. Located in Sajjangarh Biological Park; entry fee for both park and palace. 5km west of city centre.

places.name: Jagdish Temple
places.description: Large 17th-century Indo-Aryan temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Jagannath), 150m from the City Palace main gate. Features a large brass Garuda (eagle) at the entrance, intricate relief carvings and elephant sculptures. Active pilgrimage temple; aarti held morning and evening. Free entry.

places.name: Saheliyon-ki-Bari
places.description: 18th-century ornamental garden built by Maharana Sangram Singh II for his queen's 48 handmaidens. Features fountains, marble pavilions, kiosks, elephant and lion statues, and a lotus pool. Compact garden; visit in early morning before heat. Budget 30–45 minutes.

places.name: Bagore Ki Haveli
places.description: 18th-century haveli on the Gangaur Ghat lakefront, now a museum displaying royal costumes, turbans, puppets and antiques across 138 rooms. Hosts an evening cultural show (Dharohar) of Rajasthani folk dance and music at 19:00 (Jul–Mar) and 19:00 (Apr–Jun). Combined museum and show ticket available.

places.name: Ambrai Ghat
places.description: Sunset-watching ghat on the Ambrai bank of Lake Pichola offering the classic Udaipur view: City Palace and Lake Palace reflected in still water. Free viewpoint; the adjacent Ambrai restaurant is popular for lakeside dinner. Best photographed in golden hour 30 minutes before sunset.

places.name: Shiv Niwas Palace
places.description: Semi-circular 19th-century palace at the southern end of the City Palace complex, now a heritage hotel. Interiors include silver urns, crystal and artefacts from the royal collection. Afternoon tea in the ornate Crystal Gallery drawing room is a popular option for non-guests.

places.name: Ahar Cenotaphs
places.description: Cremation ground and memorial complex of the Mewar rulers (19 generations), containing 250+ chhatris (domed cenotaphs). Adjacent to the Ahar Archaeological Museum which displays artefacts from the Ahar culture (1700–1200 BCE). Quiet, rarely crowded; free entry. 3km east of city centre.

places.name: Vintage and Classic Car Museum
places.description: Collection of vintage cars once owned by the Mewar royal family, including a 1934 Rolls Royce used during the Independence Day parade. About 22 vintage vehicles. Located near Fateh Sagar Lake; small compact museum taking about 30–45 minutes.

places.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site 84km north of Udaipur in the Aravalli hills. Features the world's second-longest wall (36km), built in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha. Birthplace of Maharana Pratap. Half-day or full-day trip from Udaipur; typically combined with Ranakpur Jain temples.

places.name: Ranakpur Jain Temples
places.description: Exquisitely carved 15th-century Jain temple complex 96km north of Udaipur, considered one of the five most sacred Jain pilgrimage sites. The main Chaturmukha Dharana Vihara temple has 1444 ornately carved pillars, no two identical. Best combined with Kumbhalgarh Fort on a full-day trip.
